metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data
supplementary_materials: available from the corresponding author upon request

hyperparameters.name: Learning rate eta
hyperparameters.context: Gradient step size for the Adam optimizer used to update weights.

hyperparameters.name: Batch size k
hyperparameters.context: Number of sampled transitions used in each training iteration.

hyperparameters.name: Decision step size L
hyperparameters.context: The fixed time interval at which signal timing actions are determined.

hyperparameters.name: Exploration rate epsilon
hyperparameters.context: Probability of taking a random action to explore new policies.

hyperparameters.name: Freeze interval F
hyperparameters.context: Step interval for updating the frozen target network parameters.

hyperparameters.name: Replay buffer size B
hyperparameters.context: Total transitions stored in the experience replay buffer for training.

hyperparameters.name: Reward weight mu
hyperparameters.context: Weight coefficient for average speed in the multi-objective reward function.

hyperparameters.name: Reward weight omega
hyperparameters.context: Weight coefficient for queue length in the multi-objective reward function.

metadata.hardware_requirements: computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China, including 10-minute traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and calibrated driving behavior parameters.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Paper states data is available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extracts vehicle position matrices (mt) from raw video frames. Includes zooming and down-sampling to a specific input size (4x512 pixels). Stacks consecutive N time steps to represent the state (st) to maintain temporal information.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, most dimensions and procedures stated, but specific vision tools for location extraction from raw pixels not named.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: Trains a dual-head CNN (multitask learning) using Deep Q-Learning (DQN). Uses Adam optimizer, epsilon-greedy exploration, experience replay, and a separate target network to stabilize training. Predicts Q-values, mean speed, and queue length simultaneously to optimize a weighted reward function.
tools_mentioned: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU version not stated
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all architecture details, hyperparameters, and optimization logic are explicitly stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator.
nodes_process.description: Evaluates the trained model against 'No control' and 'PI-ALINEA' baselines in 20 simulation experiments. Performs perturbation analysis by removing information from specific road subareas to assess model reliance on diverse visual features.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, simulator and specific scenario parameters are stated; only specific simulation versioning is missing.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments. It is found that the performance of the PI-ALINEA method is not always better than that of the no control scenario.
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of mean vehicle travel times (in seconds) across 20 simulation experiments for three scenarios: No controls, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL. Includes percentage change relative to no-control.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Inputs based on cited SUMO and empirical data; parameters in Table 1 support replication, though specific random seeds for the 20 runs are not provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Training convergence curves showing (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time in seconds over 1 million frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Network architecture and hyperparameters provided; raw training data based on real-world observations. Slight ambiguity in reward weight tuning.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series plot of vehicle travel times in the mainline (minutes) showing quartiles for No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios over the peak period.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Procedure and inputs clearly defined; result directly visualizes output distributions from the described simulator setup.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing the distribution of mean speeds (m/s) across time (8:00-9:00) and distance (0-4000m) for (a) no-control, (b) PI-ALINEA, and (c) DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visual representation of simulator state; depends on specific trajectory logging in SUMO which is mostly specified.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Queue length (meters) over time at the on-ramp for three control scenarios, showing interquartile ranges.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Inputs and aggregation method (quartiles) are clearly specified based on standard simulation outputs.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on ramp and the red ratios... in each simulation for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plot with regression lines showing the relationship between red ratio (%) and queue length (m) for PI-ALINEA and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Plausible derivation from logs, though 'red ratio' calculation over specific cycles is summarized.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of downstream traffic volume (veh/h) sampled at 5-minute intervals for No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Standard volume extraction from simulation; consistency with reported mainline improvements.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Box plot comparison of travel times under different perturbation scenarios (removing input data from subareas 1-8) compared to baseline.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Perturbation method described, but specific 'removal' mechanics (masking vs zeroing) of position matrix data are partially specified.
